text.p: Twenty three people died in two days of clashes between cattle rearers fighting over grazing land in northeastern Nigeria, witnesses said on Saturday.
The clashes, between Fulani cattle farmers and migrant Udawa cattle rearers from near the Chadian border, started on Thursday and were not brought under control until Friday. they said.
"Nineteen of those killed are Fulani and four are Udawa," said Sanka Mohammed, a journalist in Laushin-Daji, the scene of the clashes in the Yamaltu-Deba local government area of Gombe state.
The combatants used guns and bows and arrows. More than 100 huts were burnt and scores of cattle, sheep and goats killed.
Residents said fighting broke out when the migrant cattle rearers arrived in an area already demarcated for grazing and farming by the Fulani.
The ward head, Jauro Mai-Unguwa said clashes occur annually at the onset of the rainy season when migrant cattle rearers move south in search of grazing land.
"This thing happens yearly and it is high time the government did something to check it," said Mai-Unguwa.
Gombe state police headquarters in Gombe town declined to comment on the clashes but said riot police had moved in and restored order.
